newsitem.title: USA: News Corp's Murdoch vows satellite to go ahead - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: News Corp's Murdoch vows satellite to go ahead - WSJ.

text.p: News Corp Chairman Rupert Murdoch vowed to continue with plans to launch a satellite-television service, despite recent suggestions a $1 billion deal with EchoStar Communications was unravelling, the Wall Street Journal said.

"We're going ahead, either on our own or with (EchoStar Chairman Charlie Ergen) if he meets the terms of the contract," Murdoch was quoted in the newspaper's electronic edition on Friday as saying in a telephone interview.
EchoStar said at the start of the week it was delaying regulatory filings on the venture over News Corp's demands it abandon a conditional-access system it used.
Charlie Ergen, EchoStar's chairman, said on April 29 he planned to honor the agreement with News Corp.
In an interview, the Journal also reported Murdoch said he did not fire Preston Padden, the head of News Corp's so-called ASkyB satellite-TV who just announced his resignation.
"We want to keep him," Murdoch was quoted as telling the Journal by telephone. "We think he is a terrific piece of manpower."
Murdoch declined comment on recent reports he might try to team up with other cable operators like Tele-Communications and Time Warner, the Journal said.
